title: Streams with title names
context: Join watch events to the catalogue.
task: Set result to streams merged with titles on title_id, keeping stream_id, title, genre, minutes_watched.

title: Minutes per genre
task: Set result to a Series of total minutes_watched per genre, sorted descending.

title: Most watched title
task: Set result to the title (str) with the highest total minutes_watched.

title: Completion rate per genre
task: Set result to a Series of mean completed per genre (2 dp), sorted descending.

title: Named aggregations
task: Set result to a DataFrame indexed by genre with columns streams (count) and minutes (sum of minutes_watched), sorted by genre.

title: Minutes per user
task: Set result to a Series of total minutes_watched per user_id, sorted descending.

title: Minutes per country
task: Set result to a Series of total minutes_watched per user country, sorted descending.

title: Users who never streamed
task: Set result to the number of users with no rows in streams (an int).

title: Titles never watched
task: Set result to a Series of title (names) with no rows in streams.

title: Streams per weekday
task: Set result to a Series of stream counts per weekday name (from watch_date), ordered Mon..Sun.

title: Weekend viewing share
task: Set result to the percentage of streams on Sat/Sun rounded to 1 decimal.

title: Session length bucket
task: Set result to a Series of stream counts per session bucket using pd.cut on minutes_watched with bins [0,15,45,90,200] and labels ['<15','15-45','45-90','90+'].
hint: pd.cut then value_counts sorted by index.
answer:
b = pd.cut(streams['minutes_watched'], bins=[0, 15, 45, 90, 200], labels=['<15', '15-45', '45-90', '90+'])
result = b.value_counts().sort_index()

title: Active days per user
task: Set result to a Series of the number of distinct watch dates per user_id, sorted descending.

title: Binge days
task: Set result to the number of (user, day) pairs with 3 or more distinct titles watched (an int).

title: Genre by device pivot
task: Set result to pd.crosstab of genre (rows) vs device (columns) counting streams.
answer:
m = streams.merge(titles, on='title_id')
result = pd.crosstab(m['genre'], m['device'])

title: Minutes by plan and device
task: Set result to a pivot_table: index plan, columns device, values sum of minutes_watched, fill_value 0.
answer:
m = streams.merge(users, on='user_id')
result = m.pivot_table(index='plan', columns='device', values='minutes_watched', aggfunc='sum', fill_value=0)

title: Monthly revenue
task: Set result to a Series of total amount per subscription month ('YYYY-MM'), sorted by month.

title: Active subs per month
task: Set result to a Series of distinct user_id count per month ('YYYY-MM'), sorted by month.

title: Completion label
task: Set result to streams with a column status: 'Finished' if completed==1 else 'Dropped'.

title: Average completion by kind
task: Set result to a Series of mean completed by title kind (2 dp).

title: Top 3 genres per device
task: Set result to a DataFrame device, genre, minutes for the top 3 genres by minutes within each device, sorted by device then minutes desc.
answer:
m = streams.merge(titles, on='title_id')
g = m.groupby(['device', 'genre'])['minutes_watched'].sum().reset_index(name='minutes')
result = g.sort_values(['device', 'minutes'], ascending=[True, False]).groupby('device').head(3).reset_index(drop=True)

title: Repeat viewers
context: Users watching the same title 2+ times.
task: Set result to the number of (user, title) pairs watched 2 or more times (an int).

title: Days since signup to first stream
task: Set result to a Series (indexed by user_id) of days from signup_date to first watch_date, for users who streamed.
hint: first watch per user, merge signup, subtract.

title: Watch fraction
context: How much of a title was watched.
task: Set result to streams merged with titles plus a column frac = minutes_watched / runtime_min rounded to 2 dp; keep stream_id, frac.
answer:
m = streams.merge(titles, on='title_id')
m['frac'] = (m['minutes_watched'] / m['runtime_min']).round(2)
result = m[['stream_id', 'frac']]

title: Over-watched streams
task: Set result to the number of streams where minutes_watched exceeds the title's runtime_min (an int).
answer:
m = streams.merge(titles, on='title_id')
result = int((m['minutes_watched'] > m['runtime_min']).sum())

title: Busiest watch date
task: Set result to the watch_date (as a Timestamp) with the most streams.

title: Average sessions per active user
task: Set result to the mean number of streams per user among users who streamed, rounded to 2 dp.

title: Kids content by young users
task: Set result to the number of streams of 'Kids' genre titles by users aged under 18 (an int).
answer:
m = streams.merge(titles, on='title_id').merge(users, on='user_id')
result = int(((m['genre'] == 'Kids') & (m['age'] < 18)).sum())

title: Genre popularity by country
task: Set result to a Series indexed by country giving the most-streamed genre in that country.
hint: merge all three, groupby country+genre size, idxmax per country.
answer:
m = streams.merge(titles, on='title_id').merge(users, on='user_id')
g = m.groupby(['country', 'genre']).size()
result = g.groupby(level=0).idxmax().apply(lambda t: t[1])

title: Fill missing minutes
task: Set result to streams (merged with titles genre) with minutes_watched missing values filled by the genre median; keep stream_id, genre, minutes_watched.
answer:
m = streams.merge(titles[['title_id', 'genre']], on='title_id')
m['minutes_watched'] = m['minutes_watched'].fillna(m.groupby('genre')['minutes_watched'].transform('median'))
result = m[['stream_id', 'genre', 'minutes_watched']]

title: Months subscribed per user
task: Set result to a Series of the number of subscription months per user_id, sorted descending.

title: Lifetime value per user
task: Set result to a Series of total amount paid per user_id, sorted descending.

title: Average watch fraction per genre
task: Set result to a Series of mean (minutes_watched / runtime_min) per genre, rounded to 2 dp, sorted descending.
hint: merge, compute frac, groupby genre mean.
answer:
m = streams.merge(titles, on='title_id')
m['frac'] = m['minutes_watched'] / m['runtime_min']
result = m.groupby('genre')['frac'].mean().round(2).sort_values(ascending=False)
